paper: Towards Better Evaluation for Dynamic Link Prediction (EdgeBank)
main_claim: Memorization baseline (EdgeBank) matches or outperforms complex temporal GNNs due to high edge repetition and easy negative sampling.
closest_relation_to_our_work: Direct comparison baseline for exact edge memory.
potential_overlap: Memorization of past interacting pairs as prediction signal.
key_difference: EdgeBank only performs exact edge lookup; does not model evolving community structure, does not study conflicting distractor durations (T_B), and does not evaluate historical regime retrieval.

paper: Future Link Prediction Without Memory or Aggregation (CRAFT)
main_claim: Temporal link prediction can achieve state-of-the-art without recurrent memory or neighborhood aggregation via cross-attention.
closest_relation_to_our_work: Challenges necessity of online recurrent memory.
potential_overlap: Argues online recurrent memory is fragile and costly.
key_difference: CRAFT evaluates general future link prediction on static/drift datasets; does not investigate historical recoverability under recurring regimes (A->B->A).

paper: Temporal Graph Networks for Deep Learning on Dynamic Graphs (TGN)
main_claim: Continuous-time GNN combining per-node recurrent memory state updated by events with temporal graph attention.
closest_relation_to_our_work: Primary architecture under study for recurrent degradation.
key_difference: TGN assumes stationary or smoothly drifting graphs; we show TGN recurrent states undergo destructive overwriting during conflicting distractor regimes.

paper: Inductive Representation Learning on Temporal Graphs (TGAT)
main_claim: Self-attention over temporal neighborhoods using continuous time encoding without persistent node memory.
potential_overlap: Uses time-aware attention over recent neighbors.
key_difference: TGAT only samples local recent temporal neighbors; cannot retrieve historical regimes beyond temporal truncation window.

paper: Predicting Dynamic Embedding Trajectory in Temporal Interaction Networks (JODIE)
main_claim: Coupled RNN updates user and item embeddings on interaction and projects trajectory into future.
closest_relation_to_our_work: Recurrent state updates in continuous time.
key_difference: JODIE's recurrent projection is vulnerable to state overwriting under non-stationary distractor intervals.

closest_relation_to_our_work: Recurrent state formulation for dynamic graphs.
key_difference: Does not study regime recurrence or measure recoverability as a function of distractor duration.

paper: Inductive Representation Learning on Temporal Graphs through Temporal Walks (CAW)
main_claim: Causal anonymous walks capture network motifs and structural temporal patterns without persistent memory.
key_difference: CAW relies on causal temporal walk sampling bounded to recent history; does not retrieve disconnected past historical regimes.

paper: Overcoming Catastrophic Forgetting in Graph Continual Learning (ER-GNN)
main_claim: Experience replay buffer of representative nodes mitigates catastrophic forgetting across sequential graph tasks.
closest_relation_to_our_work: Continual learning and historical knowledge retention.
potential_overlap: Use of episodic memory buffers to combat forgetting.
key_difference: ER-GNN evaluates task-incremental node classification across disjoint tasks; does not evaluate continuous-time link prediction or parameterize distractor duration (T_B).

paper: Continual Graph Learning with Temporal Distribution Shift
main_claim: Decouples invariant structural trends from time-varying distribution shifts to maintain performance on evolving graphs.
closest_relation_to_our_work: Studies distribution shifts over dynamic graphs.
key_difference: Focuses on monotonic evolution and domain shift; does not isolate controlled recurring regimes (A->B->A) or addressable snapshot retrieval.

paper: GraphMixer: Simplified Architecture for Temporal Graph Representation Learning
main_claim: Simple MLP-based mixer over temporal links outperforms complex GNN and memory architectures.
closest_relation_to_our_work: Memory-free baseline demonstrating simplicity of link prediction.
key_difference: Fixed temporal window aggregation forgets past regimes once they fall outside the mixer context.

potential_overlap: Historical sequence modeling for temporal links.
key_difference: DyGFormer truncates sequence length to recent $N$ events ($N \le 64$)

paper: Towards Better Dynamic Graph Learning: A Survey
main_claim: Comprehensive taxonomy of temporal graph models, memory mechanisms, and evaluation benchmarks.
closest_relation_to_our_work: Taxonomy of memory vs memory-free temporal methods.
key_difference: Identifies memory loss as a theoretical challenge but notes absence of controlled recurrence benchmarks.

paper: Streaming Graph Neural Networks via Continual Subgraph Replay
main_claim: Maintains dynamic reservoir of informative subgraphs to prevent forgetting during streaming graph updates.
closest_relation_to_our_work: Sub-graph memory buffer for streaming graphs.
key_difference: Focuses on replay for gradient updates in continuous learning; does not study addressable retrieval during regime recurrence.
